utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No preliminaries were announced. Therefore, we're waiting for the witness to be escorted in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But that's no reason not to have the case called. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you. And good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President, Your Honours. I just, as the witness is being brought in, ask that 65 ter 32300 be called up. Page 40.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I meanwhile also use the time in relation to one item, it's the testimony of Goran Krcmar. In relation to P7172, which was marked for identification pending a translation, the Chamber would like to receive an update from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Blagojevic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Blagojevic, I remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration you have given yesterday at the beginning of your testimony. Ms. Hasan will now continue her cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Blagojevic.

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Just to touch on -- to make a final point on what we were discussing yesterday, and I'm going to read to you one more thing that said during your testimony in the Karadzic case, and this is in relation to the shells that were fired on the Srebrenica enclave on the 25th of May 1995. And that is: You will recall me reading to you an excerpt where you discussed whether you assumed responsibility for the firing of those shells, and you said, and this is at line 22 of your Karadzic testimony, you said --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We don't have it on the screen yet.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Page 40 of 65 ter 32300.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It's there now. Please proceed, Ms. Hasan.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: So line 22, and I'll read this to you, it says you say: "It was not my decision. I was implementing an immediate order. There is no two ways about it. It is very clear in military terms." So I just want to be very clear what your position is. Do you stand by the testimony you gave there in the Karadzic case?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if we can turn to 65 ter 32297, please. And what you will see here is -- it's an interim report of the 28th Division of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and it's dated the 26th of May. You can take -- have a read through it.

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have read it.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: So it's talking about the 25th of May and that the enemy has shelled the area of Srebrenica and Suceska and that at 1900 hours, two 82-millimetre mortar shells fell near the primary school, and it goes on to talk about the shelling of Suceska, and it sets out the casualties as a result of that shelling. Now, did you authorise your units that day to fire mortars onto the Srebrenica enclave?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Is it possible that the impact of the howitzers that were fired were mistaken for 82-millimetre mortar shells.

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I doubt it. This report refers to a completely different area. The distance is significant from one place to the other.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Okay. But leaving aside the locations, would you say and your -- would you say that just the -- that the impact of the howitzers could have been mistaken for impact of 82-millimetre mortar shells?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would never take one for the other. No, I cannot say anything about what might happen to others.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Okay. I'll move onto the next document.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: If I could offer then 65 ter 32297 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you have the intention to tender the document which is on the screen now?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P7257, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And you will recall that this document notes that the two mortar shells were fired at -- at 1900 hours, and you will recall the document we looked at yesterday where it says the howitzers were fired at 1907 hours. You recall that; right?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is that a question for me?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think you're right on that at all. If you look at the previous document, the one that you showed me yesterday, you will see --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, you may have misunderstood the question. The question is whether you recall that what the document says was shown to you yesterday, the document saying that howitzers were fired at seven minutes past 7.00 in the evening. Do you recall that that document has been shown to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. If we could look at 65 ter 25386, please. What will appear is a June 7, 1995, UNPROFOR report. And if we could, for the time being, turn to page 7 in the English, page 9 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And I'll turn your attention to item C.1. And it starts in the English just at the bottom of the page. This is a report on crater analysis, and it records under that item, we see time A and time B, that there's an impact between 1915 hours and 1925 hours. The first two digits, 25, being the date; 25 May 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And if we turn the page in the English.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: We see UNPROFOR here recording that this impact resulted -- it says under item 5, "Type of weapon: Artillery, 105-millimetre." You see that?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We cannot hear the speaker. Witness, could you please adjust your microphone that when you are leaning over towards the screen that you can still be heard, yes. Perhaps the -- could you please repeat your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see paragraph 5 on the right-hand side. It says RT 105 millimetres.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now it records the casualties as well, and these are the same casualties we saw in the ABiH report. Fatima Dautbasic, and I'm probably mispronouncing that, as well as Ms. Mustafic Nusreta, both of whom were injured as a result of this firing. Now just below you see under D.1, again time -- 25th of May, date; time, between 1918 hours and 1935 hours. In the B/C/S we can turn to the next page. Mr. Blagojevic, if you just look under D.1 towards the top of that page you see the times there and the date of another impact, and UNPROFOR records that: "The impact was on the wall of a wood store and we couldn't analyse properly but we suspect it came from the same direction as above. "Artillery used: 105 millimetre." Now if we turn to page 11 in the English and page 14 in the B/C/S, and you will recall the document we looked at yesterday, P7255, this was the interim combat report in your name for the 25th of May where it records that two of the shells were observed and the other two were not. Here, on this page, under item 3, you see Team Srebrenica. And (B), under (B), UNPROFOR records that: "It was reported to UNMOs at 262930," and that's a reference -- sorry. "It reported to UNMOs," there's some digits there by a police officer, "that there was shelling in Bucinovici between 1905 and 1915 hours yesterday," that being the 25th of May. "Casualties were brought to Srebrenica hospital, including girl, 9 years old, killed; Gabelic Jasna, Almaz, injured; 12 years old girl, Gabelic, Alma, Almaz, with left arm broken. UNMO team was not able to carry out investigation due to the ROM in that area imposed by the BiH." Now, that corresponds to what we saw in the ABiH report. Now, the two howitzers that were fired at 1907 hours that were not observed, those shells are the ones that fell on this village of Bucinovici; isn't that the case?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot agree with what you said, because yesterday we stated that 105-millimetre artillery pieces fired in the area of Srebrenica, fired four shells. This does not correspond to what you are asking me about, and I cannot confirm anything. Because Bucinovici - I don't know exactly according to the map - but they're probably at some distance. Now, we could see how far away that is from Srebrenica, if I could take a look at a map.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Well, I can tell that you that's in the area of Suceska. But let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I'd offer 65 ter 25386 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P7258, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And you would be aware, wouldn't you, that around the same time shortly after 7.00 p.m. on the 25th of May when your units fired howitzers at the inhabited enclave of Srebrenica, that the centre of Tuzla was also shelled and that 66 young individuals, young persons were killed?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that. I did not know about it then. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Well, this was the first day you took office as Bratunac Brigade commander. And it was also Youth Day celebrated in the region. So you don't recall a massive shelling of the centre of Tuzla with scores of casualties? You were unaware of that event?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unaware of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Let's take a look at 65 ter 25386, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I'm sorry, it's the document we are looking at, and if I can just turn to page 3 in the English and in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: It's a report on the shelling that took place. And it reads: "As a sequel to the air strikes administered by NATO at Pale ammo dump, Bosnian Serb army resorted to massive retaliatory artillery shelling against Tuzla town and TAB. It's our position that that refers to the Tuzla air base which is considered deliberate targeting of UN troops, tps, and Tuzla safe area. The shelling commenced at 1910 hours simultaneously at Tuzla air base and the Tuzla safe area. ... total of 31 impacts were recorded up till 2100 hours." Just the last sentence of that paragraph: "66 people were massacred to death and 170 were wounded, amongst them 31 were critically injured." Sir, you were not aware that at approximately almost exactly the same time that you fired into Srebrenica there was concerted firing at Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I'd offer 25386 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It's already admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We admitted it a minute ago. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: The next document, 65 ter 17696, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And, in fact, Mr. Blagojevic, not only was Srebrenica attacked at that time on that day, not only was Tuzla attacked, but so were the safe areas of Gorazde and Bihac, as was Sarajevo. We see here a code cable, UN code cable, dated the 26th of May, 1995, subject: "Air strikes Sarajevo." And it reads or starts off reading: "After the air strikes [sic] of 25 May 1995, all safe areas less Zepa have been shelled and Bosnian Serbs have fired heavy weapons from five weapon collection points around Sarajevo." You see that there?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And, in fact, Mr. Blagojevic, you must have known that all the safe areas, including Srebrenica which your units fired at, less Zepa were fired at at that very same day?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Regardless of the fact that you say that I had to know, I did not know.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We didn't hear the end of the sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you repeat the last part of your answer. You said you didn't know. And what did you then add?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm saying that regardless of the fact that the Prosecutor says that I had to know, I did not know about that. I assure you of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Hasan.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I'd offer 65 ter 17696 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P7259, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, let's move onto 65 ter 062 -- I'm sorry. 06288, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And this is an order from General Zivanovic. It's dated the 25th of May, 1995, and it was received, appears, from -- by the Rogatica Brigade at 0020 hours on the 26th. Now, it's addressed to the commands of, amongst others, the Bratunac Infantry Brigade. And Zivanovic provides here that: "On 25 May 1995 in the afternoon the NATO aircrafts within the UNPROFOR contingent fired at the facilities of the Army of Republika Srpska. The Army of Republika Srpska responded accordingly with the activities against the selected targets." Sir, does this order refresh your recollection about the events of 25 May and that the action -- and the actions your units -- units of the Bratunac Brigade took that day, that this was a concerted attack?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I don't see that this was sent to the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade. Where would I find that? Could you please point me to the place, because I can't see it?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: If you just look under where it says very urgent, command, and then it says to the command --

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: You see that?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And the second to last acronym on the first line there. You see it?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It says the 1st pbr. Usually in documents like this, the abbreviation for my brigade should be brlpbr. I don't know whether this is a mistake. However, if you look at other documents, you will see that that is the abbreviation that stands for my brigade. This may be it as well, but the customary abbreviation is 1.vrlpbr. I can't see the letter L here.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Okay, Mr. Blagojevic. Do you know of another Bratunac infantry brigade that the Drina Corps would be addressing this order to?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no other Bratunac Infantry Brigade. There was just one, the 1st Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade, and that brigade was under my command.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I'd offer 65 ter 06288 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before we do that, would the Bratunac Infantry Brigade on the fourth line be a duplication? I see it says "brpbr."

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe you're referring to the Birac, reference to the Birac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There's also a Birac Brigade, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P7260, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, you made the Drina Corps aware, as we saw in the previous documents we looked at yesterday, of the shelling, the firing into the Srebrenica enclave. That's right?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And if we look at 65 ter 15409, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: What you will see, it's a Main Staff report. It's to the president of Republika Srpska. It's reporting on the situation in the battle-field. And under item 1 where it's discussing in the SRK area of responsibility, if we look in the English just three lines down from the bottom. In the B/C/S, Mr. Blagojevic, if you look at the first full paragraph under item 1, just the last few lines there. It reads: "He fired from the NATO aircrafts (using air bombs) against the area of Jahorinski Potok, over the warehouse of the 27th Logistics Base at a distance of 500 metres." And that's a reference to the -- the NATO bombing we've been discussing. If we turn to page 4 in the English, please, and page --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we first clarify who "he" is in this context? "He fired," it said.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I believe that's a reference to NATO. The previous sentence --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Let's -- let me just have a look.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Would be the enemy. We can see in the first line there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: First line, it's "enemy." Then second sentence starts with "he fired." And then, "He fired from the NATO aircrafts." The enemy was firing from NATO aircrafts, is that...?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: That's how it reads, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I see that. Okay. Let's move on and ...

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: If we can turn to page 4 in the English and B/C/S page 3, the Main Staff is reporting on the activities in the Drina Corps area of responsibility. This is under item 6. It's in the middle of the page in the B/C/S. And under 6(B), situation in the corps, the Main Staff reports: "Enemy fire was timely returned against observed targets. All the corps units are in the level of readiness as ordered. Artillery was used against the enclaves Srebrenica and Gorazde and Tuzla airport."

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: You see that, Mr. Blagojevic?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And you'd agree that the information that you provided to the Drina Corps was relayed to the Main Staff and to the president of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When it comes to the artillery attack, I can see that the information was relayed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I'd offer 65 ter 15409 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P7261, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7261 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Blagojevic, I'm going to move a little bit in time to the 6th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And I'd like to turn to 65 ter 32320, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And what will you see here, it's a report, and it's from Drina Corps Commands to the command of the air force and anti-aircraft defence. And it's requesting -- it says: "We would like to request your permission ..."

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I am sorry, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Just so that I'm clear, and Mr. Blagojevic, it's the second telegram there at the bottom of the page. There's two on a single page. The one we're interested in is the bottom one, confidential number 21/7-501.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You should also state the date of that telegram.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Yes, it's dated 8 March, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And it reads: "We would like to request your permission to take over for the needs of the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade, which has manufactured launchers, the following materiel and technical equipment from the air force and anti-aircraft defence ..." And the items requested include a FAB-50. Can you tell us what that is?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have an explanation. I'm not an expert, not in this matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Blagojevic, if you know what it stands for, even without being an expert, you're invited to tell us. If you say, I've no idea what FAB stands for, then we'll move on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. I don't know. The time is 1994, so I really can't say anything.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: It's our position, Mr. Blagojevic, that that's a fabricated air bomb, 50 kilograms. Now, it also reads in this document that the Bratunac Brigade has manufactured launchers. What are those manufactured launchers?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I can tell you in very general terms is this. Vehicles were prepared. Some devices were mounted on them to be used to launch certain devices. However, while I was there, I don't think I had those things. I don't remember. But every now and then I did see such things when I was in other positions, not only when I was a brigade commander. I can't tell you anything about its operation function, how it's activated. I really can't tell you anything with any certainty.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Okay. And when you're talking about -- just to help us out here, when you're talking about some devices were mounted on the vehicles, can you be a little bit more specific and describe that for us?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How should I do that? I've told you everything. I'm not expert for that technology. I can't describe anything. I can just imagine things, but my imagination would not reflect the truth of the matter, and I'm not willing to do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Okay. We'll come back to this, Mr. Blagojevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: If we can have a look at D303, please. And as that comes up, I'll just deal with the last document, 32320, and offer that into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P7262, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And, Mr. Blagojevic, you're familiar with this document. It's the order for active combat operations dated the 5th of July, 1995. Part of the Krivaja 95 attack plan. Now, if we turn to page 4 in the B/C/S and page 4 in the English, please. And as we know, this is your document, Mr. Blagojevic, which you testified about yesterday and told us that you compiled. Under item -- under tasks, item 6.2, it reads: "The 128-millimetre launcher platoon will provide support from the fire position in the Kaolin sector. "At 0300 hours on 6 July, 1995, it will fire four projectiles (50 kilogram air bombs) on the Potocari sector (the school, the 11th March factory, the Gracic hill, TT-377, Kula, and Orici)." You see that, Mr. Blagojevic?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And I don't know if this helps you, but would these 50 kilogram air bombs, "avio bombe" in your language, be the same 50-kilogram air bombs we just -- the same type of 50-kilogram air bombs we saw in the previous document, or do you believe those are two different types of air bombs?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say anything with any certainty but I can see that we're talking about the 128-millimetre launcher platoon. I really can't tell you what kind of bombs they had. I know that they were the 128-millimetre launcher platoon, but I don't know anything about the bombs.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Blagojevic, this is your -- this is your order. You ordered this task --

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: -- to this platoon, and I take it you understood very well what you were referring to when you ordered the firing of four 50-kilogram air bombs into Potocari, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is part of my order; I understand that.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Well, let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Let's look at 65 ter 04217, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And this, Mr. Blagojevic, is another one of your daily combat reports. It's dated the following day, the 6th of July, 1995 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Could you repeat the number, please, just for the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And if could I ask that we turn to the handwritten version of this report, which is page 2 in the -- sorry, page 3 in the B/C/S and page 2 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And for your benefit, Mr. Blagojevic, we can move to page 3 -- 4 in the B/C/S, so you can just see the end of that handwritten document. Okay?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: If we just turn back a page so we can look at the content of this daily combat report that goes to the Drina Corps. Back a page just in the B/C/S, please. It reads under item 2, just the second paragraph in the English: "Firing support against set targets was provided by 70-millimetre shell launcher (school in Potocari, 11 Mart factory, and wide area of the village of Potocari)." Are you following, Mr. Blagojevic.

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: So these 70-millimetre shell launchers, what are -- what is that?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 128-millimetre a while ago and now 70-millimetre, the two figures should be the same. They're not, and I find that surprising. This should be one and the same: 128-millimetre launcher platoon, because there is no other such unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: All right. But this is talking about shell launchers. What -- what is that a reference to?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And it's "shell launcher," in quotation marks. Could you tell us what that refers to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This could only refer to the 128-millimetre launcher platoon. That's the unit that was mentioned in the order. I did not sign this specific combat report. Somebody else did it. I don't know how professionally he could portray the situation in his report so that the report reflected it properly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Could we look at the signature again at the end of the handwritten draft, please, for Mr. Blagojevic. Do you see the signature there, Mr. Blagojevic? Do you know whose that is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can see the signature, but can I also see the word "z-a," "za." I'm sure you can see that. And as for the rest, I don't know. It may have been a duty operations officer in the ops room or in the office where such documents were drafted, and he sent it in its present form.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I ask you an additional question. The handwriting of the text, I'm not referring to the signature, the handwriting, whose handwriting is that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The same person who is probably the duty operations officer. I don't know who else it could have been. There may have been two. Maybe one of them drafted it, the other signed it. In any case, it was the duty operations officer in the ops room who drafted it, and I don't know whether the same person signed it. At this moment, I really can't detect whose handwriting this could be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And I have -- is there any fact to your knowledge which could explain while -- why the words "shell launcher" are put in quotation marks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, there's no rule to that effect. It's just something people did. Representatives of the people, an armed formation. Maybe this is just one of the popular expressions that you sometimes find in texts that should be written in a proper military professional form. I really can't tell you. I don't know. I have no explanation. There's every possible indication that this reference is to the 128-millimetre launcher platoon, the one that I mentioned in my order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, you are constantly referring to what is apparently a unit, whereas reading this I get the impression that it may not be a normal unit or something of the kind but that it's something special and that that's the reason why it is put in quotation marks. Do you have any comment on such an understanding of this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can only tell you that in the light infantry brigade I had a mixed artillery battery, a mixed artillery battery which comprised howitzers and a 122-millimetre launcher platoon, some cannons, and some other tools that I can't remember. The battery was mixed, and that means that it had all sorts of equipment and tools. That's why it was called a mixed artillery battery.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would it have had any launchers which would be able to fire modified air bombs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It had a 128-millimetre launcher platoon. You can see it in my order. A platoon is a lower-ranking unit than a battery. A battery is usually comprised of platoons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, my question was whether where you said that it had all sorts of equipment and tools, whether it had any launchers which would be able to fire modified air bombs? Could you please answer that question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We had a launcher platoon, a 128-millimetre launcher platoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's not an answer to my question but please proceed, Ms. Hasan.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I don't know if this will assist.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Mr. Blagojevic, when you refer to "platoon," do you mean a platform?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A platoon is an organisational unit. Usually it's a part of a company or a battery.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness clearly referred to a unit in -- a platoon is a lower-ranking unit than a battery. So he's talking about units and not about physical equipment. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Blagojevic, you had ordered the firing of the 50-kilogram air bombs. Now, were those dropped from the air?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not have such technical resources to order that something be dropped from the air, so I couldn't have done anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: So how were they fired?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A launcher platoon has artillery technical resources, how they fire artillery. I am an engineer myself. I'm not an artilleryman.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, let's be quite clear. Modified air bombs, at least we heard evidence, that they are launched on equipment which has rails, not from a tube. Because we heard evidence that modified air bombs are bombs which are used to drop from aircrafts but used on the ground, some propelling little rockets are fixed on it, and then - at least that's what some of the evidence says - they were launched by a launcher which is rails rather than tubes or barrels. In the documents that have been shown to you, reference is made to 50-kilogram bombs and in -- it's the Prosecution's position that air bombs -- these are air bombs. Now, could you tell us how such projectiles, such bombs, were fired? And if you say you're a technician, I take it that you fully understood my brief explanation of what evidence we received. Tell us how the 50-kilogram bombs were fired? And if I say, I don't know, then we'll just move on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know that technology. I really do not know ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, even this Chamber and the parties which are all trained lawyers and not technicians have shown to have at least some understanding on how it works. But you say, though being a technician, have you no idea how 50-kilogram bombs, which are referred to, are launched? You have no idea?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Hasan -- or as a matter of fact, it's time for a break. I think you've got approximately half an hour left. Is that ...

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I trust your calculation of that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, it's not my calculations only, but could you tell us whether you'd -- you're on track?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, we'll take a break. We'd like to see you back in 20 minutes. You may now follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll take a break of 20 minutes. We'll resume at five minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: While waiting for the witness to be escorted in the courtroom, I meanwhile would like to briefly deal with a remaining issue concerning the testimony of Vojo Kupresanin. It's about D853. D853 was marked for identification pending an agreement between the parties on the excerpt to be tendered, this is found at transcript page 29668 to 29669, and the Chamber would like to hear from the parties whether any agreement was reached.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I have to talk in my name and in the name of Mr. Traldi. We have the agreement, only it technically has to be cut out from the original document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. That's good. And then it will be uploaded. We'll then hear from you once that is done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Hasan, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Blagojevic, this document that we're looking at, whether it was prepared and drafted by your aide, be it a duty officer or somebody else assisting you, as the commander of the Bratunac Brigade in whose name this report goes out to the Drina Corps, you do take responsibility for this report and the contents of it; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, before I tender this document, I'm told -- I'm informed that we have located a more legible copy. You will have seen that the previous page in the B/C/S is a teletyped version which is completely illegible on the screen. It has been rescanned, and I would request permission that we replace these documents with better copies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But they have not been uploaded yet, the newly scanned version. Then we'll have it marked for identification awaiting the replacement of the teletyped page by a new, better legible copy, and that's just one of the pages of the document in its entirety.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: There's apparently also a better copy of the handwritten version of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Well, whatever, it remains the same but --

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- all in better quality.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Correct. And just one other point on the document. The handwritten English translation -- sorry, the English translation of the handwritten version of it does not say "za" as the original provides, so we will be requesting a revised English translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, it says "for commander, Colonel Vidoje Blagojevic," so it's --

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: We can keep that as is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The only, perhaps the "for" is --

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: It's fine, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's put a little bit further down, there's "commander" and then "for him." Here it says "for commander." No, but let's move on. Mr. Registrar, could you give us the number under which this document is marked for identification?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be MFI P7263, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And keeps that status until further order. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: If we can look at Exhibit P41, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: This is an UNPROFOR sitrep for 5th of July, 1995, from 1700 hours to the 6th of July, 1995, 1700 hours.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And if we turn to page 5 in the English and B/C/S, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: This is a summary of the incidents that happened on the 5th and 6th of July, 1995. And it begins with 0315 hours to 0322 hours. So this at 3.15 to 3.22 in the morning. UNPROFOR records the Bosnian Serb army fired five rockets from the vicinity of -- and I can't -- that's not legible to me, 5492. Two impacted within 300 metres south of the compound Potocari.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: In the B/C/S translation, it says "6492" instead of "5492."

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour. And looking at that it says CP 6492.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Do you see that, Mr. Blagojevic?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, number 1, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Okay. Now, it's referring here to five rockets landing within 300 metres of the Potocari compound, and this is around the time, in fact, that you had ordered the firing of the air bombs; isn't that correct? At 0300 hours.

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot confirm that. I cannot confirm that. Whether that corresponds to what I had ordered in my order, I cannot confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: You do acknowledge that your order was for the firing of the air bombs at 0300 hours?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We cannot hear the speaker.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, perhaps the usher could assist in adjusting the microphone. Could you please repeat your answer, Mr. Blagojevic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that my order was related to the 128-millimetre platoon. I don't have the exact timing in my head right now whether it corresponds to what was presented here by the observers. I cannot confirm that, no way.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Blagojevic, we just looked at your order and it was for this platoon to fire at 0300 hours on 6th July to fire air bombs, and we saw the report to the Drina Corps confirming that. Now, the UNPROFOR observes at that same time rockets landing within the area of Potocari which is where you ordered those air bombs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm afraid might be confusion because in B/C/S it says not rockets but projectiles, "projektila," so the witness might be so [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, of course --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... direct your attention --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- I do not know whether the word "rockets" receives a different interpretation. But if -- unfortunately I can't check that because if I say "rockets" I am unable to hear what the B/C/S booth will tell me, but perhaps they could tell me how they translate it when I use the word "rockets." And I move for that purpose, for one second, to the B/C/S booth. Yes. Thank you for that information. The B/C/S booth confirmed that they interpreted my use of the English word "rocket" into "rocket" in B/C/S as well. So let's just ignore for a second what it says about "projektila" in the B/C/S. Witness, if you would read for the word "projektila" the word "rocket," would that change anything in your answer, whether you could confirm that this is about the same firing as was ordered for 3.00 in the morning on that date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it seems to me that projectile and rocket can be synonymous, correspond to one another. I don't know. I'm not much of an expert either, but I think that could be the case. However, on the basis of this, this formulation, as this report is written, I cannot accept that it refers to the Bratunac Brigade because there's no reference to that. How can I accept that? And it's not exactly stated --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, you were not asked to accept anything. You were asked whether you could confirm that it was about the same and apparently you cannot confirm that. That's your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it's not the same. I mean, it's written --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, did I understand your answer well that you cannot confirm that this is about the same firing as you ordered in that other document for 3.00 in the morning at that same morning?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I cannot confirm that this is from -- well, maybe it's from somewhere else. How should I know?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You've answered my question. Please proceed, Ms. Hasan.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I'm going move onto another area, Mr. Blagojevic, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Hasan, could the B/C/S being given to CLSS for final verification of the accuracy of the translation.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: We'll do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Mr. Blagojevic, your superiors in July 1995 entrusted you with commanding various units, including units of the MUP, Main Staff units, in the phase of the search operation that took place after the fall of Srebrenica and before you were deployed to Zepa; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Let's look at P1694, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: So this is a Drina Corps proposal, and it's from Colonel Ignjat Milanovic, who we know is no longer alive. And it's dated 15th of July, 1995. Relates to the engagement of forces in searching the terrain facing Zepa and proposal. And it provides in the first paragraph, last line: "The Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade is searching the terrain as ordered and is about to come out on the ordered line." And he orders, if we look down, item 4: "The Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade shall continue to search the terrain, clear up the battle ground on the Bratunac-Konjevic Polje-Kasaba axis, and create a reserve (because they currently do not have any) for engagement at request." And then comes his proposal. And his proposal is that: "The 1st Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade commander be authorised and appointed as commander of all forces engaged in the search of terrain and clearing up the battleground east of the road (the Kasaba-Drinjaca road) because we do not have anyone in the KDK whom we could assign to the task." And, in fact, Mr. Blagojevic, this proposal was implemented, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: You would agree with me that KDK stands for the command of the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And if we now look at P1696, this is a daily combat report that goes out in your name on the 16th of July, and again we have for this document a handwritten and a teletyped version of it. And what it provides is it reports to the Drina Corps that, under item 2 -- can you see that well, Mr. Blagojevic?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's all right.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Maybe we can just zoom in on the second -- thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: So it provides, and this is midway through the English paragraph: "During the day, the brigade commander visited all units which are blocking the enemy retreat (the 1st Milici Light Infantry Brigade, units of the 65th Protection Motorised Regiment, parts of the MUP, and the 5th Engineering Battalion), defined their tasks and organised their joint action and communications ..." Are you following?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And you don't deny, in fact, that this accurately reflects your role, do you?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a supposition.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Mr. Blagojevic, I think my question was quite clear. It -- this report, in your name, provides that you went and visited all these units and that you tasked them and organised their joint action. That's accurate, isn't it? This is what you did.

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I've already told you, this is a supposition. This did not happen. It was written but it did not happen in practice. So it is a supposition. In the military, suppositions do exist. I can give you a more extensive explanation, if necessary.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I'll move on, Mr. Blagojevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Are you -- may I ask you the following, Witness. Are you really saying that such a report to the Drina Corps Command would be not true? It says that the brigade commander visited all units during that day. That this is not true what was reported to the Drina Corps Command? Is that what you are saying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it didn't happen. It's a supposition.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: That means that you reported to the Drina Corps Command a fact which was not true; correct.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Because I was not in that role. If you look at the order that I received on the following day, you will see that that is the truth. And I immediately received that order because -- actually, on that very same day I received an order, on the 16th, to organise movement towards Zepa and to go --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We didn't hear the end of the sentence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So that would be that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Could you repeat the rest -- the remainder of the sentence, the end of it. The interpreters didn't hear you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm saying that on that same day I received orders from the superior command to organise the unit and to move towards Zepa. On the 17th, in the morning, I organised the units and I moved towards Zepa. I did personally. As for this report that we're speaking about, I wrote it personally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And you are saying you were conveying an untrue information to your superior command; yes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's a supposition. In military terms, supposition; that is to say, a situation is referred to but that was not the actual outcome. The actual outcome was quite different. And that is reflected in the engagement of my unit on that day, or rather the following day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Ms. Hasan.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Mr. Blagojevic, did you refuse to take command?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never received it.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned that you received --

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Allow me, please. I somehow think that I'm giving incomplete answers because Milanovic, Ignjat, lieutenant-colonel, is not in a position to order me to do anything as brigade commander. He can make a proposal. It is only the corps commander or the deputy corps commander that can give me orders. Milanovic, Ignjat was an operations officer, so a lower-ranking operations officer in the corps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, let's take it step by step. Did you visit all the units which were blocking the enemy retreat? And I take them one by one. Did you visit the Milici Light Infantry Brigade units -- no, the Milici Light Infantry Brigade. Did you visit that brigade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The 65th Protection Motorised Regiment, did you visit that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you visit parts of the MUP?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You did not define any tasks for these units?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you organise their joint action and communications?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Because I don't have the possibility to do that either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, sometimes people are doing things which they are supposed not to be able to do. But I just want to focus on facts on what you did. So you're sending a report to your command just full of lies; that is, you write what you've done and you hadn't done it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Those are not lies. Those were suppositions. In military term, suppositions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If the report would have said, "I intend to visit," or "I am preparing to define tasks," then it's clear that you haven't done it yet, but the way in which it is presented here clearly says this is what I did. And if you didn't do it, then it's not the truth. And whatever you -- if you repeat five times --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I did not do all that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But then the report is completely false because it states that you were doing things. And whether you call it suppositions or whatever, the report says "this is what I did," and you didn't do it. That's your testimony.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Hasan.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Mr. Blagojevic, isn't it the case that the only reason you claim that this is a -- as you call it, a supposition, that you didn't, in fact, do what is reported here to the Drina Corps Command is because you knew -- you know that that search operation that was conducted rounded up Muslim prisoners which were killed?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not correct. I had an order from the corps command to scour the terrain. That was my order and I complied with it. I had that order. You have it. You can show it. I searched the terrain with my own brigade. That's what I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: You have testified that you -- and it's I believe also in your statement that you received an order to engage your units and you yourself moved to Zepa on the 17th of July; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: If we could briefly look at P1581, and this is under seal so it should not be broadcast.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Hasan, you referred to the statement. Could you assist us in pointing out what paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, on page 4, paragraph 14, the witness provides towards the end of that paragraph at that time, and that time is referring to when four underage children were taken to the Bratunac Brigade, that: "At that time, I was already with the majority of the Bratunac Brigade on the positions towards the enclave of Zepa."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I now better understand what you referred to. I didn't see an order, I didn't see a date, but please proceed. But a movement to Zepa, I see that in paragraph 14. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: So this is an intercepted communication from the 17th of July at 1220 hours. And it -- the communication involves Badem, which you understand to be the code-name of the Bratunac Brigade; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Micic and X. Now if we just -- in the English, it's towards the end of the page. Micic says: "I am setting off," and there's a question mark there, "with the last one. Blagojevic is at the head." Micic continues: "Blagojevic is at the head." If we turn the page in the English and scroll down in the B/C/S just so I can see if we're ... Micic continues and he says he'll pass on the information that Blagojevic has set off at the head. Micic says: "Okay then." And then there's a repetition that Blagojevic is at the head. They're having troubles --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You should move back in B/C/S one page.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Participant X was having trouble hearing the communication. So there's this repetition that Blagojevic at the head, and what Micic says on page 1, if we can go back to page 1 in the English, Micic says towards the top half of the page: "Micic: 400 have set off. "X: 400. "Micic: Yes, at 1130 hours, the start of the column. "X: What? "Micic: 1130 hours." And they go on to talk about how many buses. Now, this is a reference to you being at the head of a column that left for Zepa; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And would that be approximately the time that you would have left to Zepa?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometime around noon, as far as I can remember. On the 17th, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: How long did you remain in the Zepa area?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some 10 to 15 days. All the time while the activities lasted. I mean, the activities surrounding Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Did you return to Bratunac in the interim during those 10 to 15 days?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so. I had a tent in the forest. That's where I spent the nights.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Could I just -- could we look at 65 ter 32298, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And I'll just ask you this, Mr. Blagojevic: Before you left to Zepa on the 14th, 15th, 16th of July, did you spend your nights at your apartment in Bratunac town?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't spend those nights in my apartment in Bratunac if when you say "an apartment," you mean a normal apartment. All the time I resided next to my command office room. I had a little room where I slept next to the command office.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And, Mr. Blagojevic, just so we're clear, I'm going to --

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: If I can ask the assistance of the usher to hand the witness a pen to mark this document. This is an aerial photograph of Bratunac town. And actually, if we could zoom out so we can see the entire image.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Hasan, have you verified where north, east, west, and south is? Because it sometimes confuses us to find later out that north is at the bottom or west is at the top. Do you have any -- could you assist the witness in the orientation of this aerial image.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Witness, perhaps we can start this way. Are you able to identify where the Bratunac Brigade headquarters is?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If this here is the Kaolin facility, where this road ends --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please refrain from marking, to start with.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A pen was provided so I thought that maybe -- very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You are invited to mark anything once are you specifically requested to mark something. So the marking has now been removed again. I think you pointed at the rather large -- large structure at the right bottom part of this aerial image. And perhaps we could -- if -- is there any way that we could assist the witness but using the cursor without it yet being marked?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that would be better.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So let's see -- you see the cursor is now on the right bottom corner where there's a large structure which apparently consists of four maybe holes, I do not know, but at least four clear long structures and two just at a 90-degree angle to them, down of it. What would that be?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That would be the Kaolin tiles factory, I believe. Part of that factory was where the command of the Bratunac Brigade was accommodated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Hasan, you proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Witness, can I actually ask you to mark the command of the Bratunac Brigade on this image.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now can you use the pen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Could the usher assist.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Usher, could you assist? Because you're now specifically asked to mark the brigade's command with the pen that was provided to you. You can do it on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: You can maybe perhaps put a K so we understand that that's "command."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, it first has to be marked anyhow.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now this is moving.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Here, in the front part. Although the sign that I drew should be a bit higher. It's lower than I meant it to be originally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It can be erased again and then you can mark it again. Wait for a second. Madam Usher, could you again assist the witness. Could you please mark with a clear K the command? And perhaps put a circle around it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It doesn't stay where I want it to stay. It gets lower.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll try again. We'll try again. If you wait for a second, it will be erased again. And then please, next time put it there where you wish to put it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is now okay?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well -- now you carefully consider where to put the K, the exact spot, and then please do it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Wait for the usher, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Again, not the right spot. It's a bit too low, but it's round about there. I would prefer it to be a little bit higher in the photo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's hereby on the record. Ms. Hasan, could you please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Mr. Blagojevic, could you put an arrow and mark the road that leads to Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that this is the road.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Could you write the letters KP next to that arrow, please.

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can I just check that this is still marking on the picture itself, because it looks as if it is -- although marking on the screen, I do not know how this finally will be. The witness marked the road which goes -- which leaves the picture at the south -- or at least at the bottom left part in a diagonal direction. Could you please put the KP again but a little bit higher then. If we have two KPs, that doesn't harm, I would say.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There we are. Please proceed, Ms. Hasan.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, the -- Konjevic Polje is due west from Bratunac town.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Mr. Blagojevic, could you then also put an arrow on the road that leads to direction Srebrenica. And if you could mark it on the image itself.

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It should be here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please mark it on the picture itself, not in the grey area next to it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And just underneath the arrow, still on the picture, could you put the letter S, please.

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Just for the record, the witness has marked an S on top of the arrow.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Mr. Blagojevic, could you now circle your residence in Bratunac in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I understand that that's where you say you spent your nights in July 1995, but you do have an apartment in Bratunac town, don't you? That's what I'd like you to mark.

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, I did not have an apartment. If you look at a document, I'm sure you have it in your archives, you will see that the apartment that my predecessor had used on my order was sealed and empty. You have that document. There was nobody living in that apartment at that time. I wish to say something else. It was only sometime towards the end of August that I reactivated that apartment when I returned from Zepa that year.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Just for the record, Ms. Hasan, when you invited the witness to mark his apartment, he put a circle around the K which he earlier marked, although a little bit too low, for the command. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: So in August and subsequent to August, you unsealed your apartment. Could you mark where that apartment is in Bratunac town, please.

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it's here. Again, this is moving and my pen keeps sliding down. It's about 5 or 6, or 7 millimetres higher. This is where the marking should actually be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I'd offer the marked image --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please, I just want you to know, I want to be precise in saying that the apartment, as the apartment to which I came and where I was, started functioning as my apartment as of the end of August 1995. Not before that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you told us already, Mr. Blagojevic, and we're carefully listening to every word you say. Mr. Registrar --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- the aerial image marked by the witness receives number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P7264, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence with the caveat that the witness corrected slightly some of the markings. Ms. Hasan, in ten minutes it will be time for the break, and two minutes ago you had used your two hours.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, it has been a bit slower than I anticipated. I would say with your indulgence if could I have 15 minutes, I can complete the area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, then try. But next time, try to not spend five minutes in court telling us where the road to Konjevic Polje is. That's typically a matter which you could agree upon with the Defence because that -- I couldn't imagine that there would be any dispute about these kind of things. Please proceed and try to keep the pace.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Mr. Blagojevic, you recall that the command post of your 1st Battalion was located in the Magasici area?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And that's along the Bratunac-Konjevic Polje road, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A bit further away from that road.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And it's less than 400 metres, you'd agree, from Glogova?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Around half a kilometre away from that road.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, when you were -- came back from Zepa, you were at the brigade command in September and October 1995?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was always at the brigade command. The question is where that command was.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: In September and October, you attended meetings at the brigade command in Bratunac town; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it could happen. My whole brigade was in the zone of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps, so that could have happened, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I'd like to look at P1516.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, in view of one of your previous answers, you said, well, the question is where that command was. Did it move from the place you marked on the aerial image to any other location in the months Ms. Hasan referred to? That's September/October. Or was it still on the same location as you have marked?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The infrastructure remained in one place in the Kaolin tile manufacturing company, but I organised my command in a different area, in the area of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps, and I took all the necessary equipment, including the communications equipment, with me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Hasan, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: You see here, Mr. Blagojevic, this is the journal of -- reports of meetings of the 1st Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade, and this is an excerpt of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: If we can turn to page 2 in the B/C/S and English, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And this is a record of the working meeting of commander with Command Staff and battalion commanders. And this meeting took place on 16 October 1995 at 0800 hours. It starts off: "Colonel Blagojevic..." You attended that meeting?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably. That's what it says here, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And if we look down, you will see the name Nikolic. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, that was Momir Nikolic; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly. Let's assume that it's him.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Well, there's evidence in this case that it's Momir Nikolic. And he reports at this meeting, the very bottom in the English: "We are currently engaged in tasks issued by the Army of Republika Srpska Main Staff (hygiene and sanitation measures)," in your language, "asanacija." Do you recall Momir Nikolic reporting at this meeting that tasks had been issued by the Main Staff, the task of "asanacija"?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, I don't seem to remember. But I can explain why.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, Witness, if you don't remember, then you don't remember. Please proceed, Ms. Hasan.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Allow me just to say this because it's very important. It's very important. As far as Momir Nikolic is concerned, everything is important. Allow me, please, to say this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, if it is about the question, that is, whether have you any recollection, you may explain. But if it's beyond that, to say --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed. Yes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we look at the agenda up here, above the name, Nikolic, it's quite clear what the agenda of that meeting was. That's very important. And now what is written here? I don't know. Sanitisation is a normal combat operation as far as I'm concerned. It is very well-known what kind of measures that entails, and that was not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, it is not relevant for the answer to your question. You said, I don't remember. Okay. That's it. And when you start drawing all kind of conclusions, we are more interested in what you do remember and what the facts are. Please proceed, Ms. Hasan.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Asanacija, Mr. Blagojevic, you knew that that was the name for the reburial operation that was taking place in the Bratunac area where bodies were removed from existing graves, taken through Bratunac town, passed your command, passed your apartment, and buried elsewhere. You knew that, didn't you? That couldn't have escaped you.

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know that. How can that be sanitisation? What do you mean by "sanitisation"? That, what are you saying now, how can I agree with you on that? How can that mean sanitisation? Then that is re-sanitisation.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And you agree, then, that re-sanitisation meant the reburial of hundreds and hundreds of bodies to conceal the crimes that had been committed?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot speak to you about that because I don't have any facts available.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have one final matter to go into. We'll just take ... I think can I complete it before the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It's time for the break. But if you say can you complete it within a few minutes, then you're invited to do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And for this, could we briefly go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. I do understand that Mr. Mladic is consulting with counsel. I have -- first of all, we'll take a break. We'd like to see you back after the break, assuming, Mr. Lukic, that you have further questions for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'd like to see you back in 20 minutes. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I'd briefly deal with two short matters, the one ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand that P7263 is marked for identification but has been uploaded now under what 65 ter number? That's the better version, both handwriting and ...

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: It's the same 65 ter number, 04271.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7263 is admitted into evidence. I further received a short report on the verification of some of the transcript of the witness's testimony in the Karadzic case. It -- I advise you to look at it carefully because it may make a difference. There is some relevant corrections in that transcript, so that you don't miss it. We'll ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It will be forwarded to you by Mr. Registrar without delay. I will -- we'll take a break, and we'll resume at 25 minutes past midday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that the parties have received the message by CLSS on the verification of the -- I think it would be fair to the witness that I briefly inform about the proposed changes. Ms. Hasan.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Just on that, Your Honours, we have listened again to the audio. And in respect of the first change that's proposed, we actually still disagree with what CLSS has come back with. And perhaps Mr. Lukic can help, because it's recorded as they say it should read he represented the Posavina command when, in fact, the B/C/S words are -- Mr. Lukic, that's your cue.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thanks. It's "ispred posavine komande," and it should be actually "ispred predpotcinjene komande."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which means?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Superior command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. I'll leave that portion then out when I inform the witness. It's -- it's a different command apparently than his own command.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's -- [Overlapping speakers] ... ORIE: And I leave that out --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Exactly what this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- until that has been settled.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But of course the other part both from the first and the second, there's no dispute about the remaining corrections?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Of course, it's not a finally settled matter but a proposal. Therefore, I'll limit myself to -- to what is also not in dispute between the parties.
