Mr. Blagojevic, you may remember that yesterday some portions of your Karadzic testimony was put to you. It was about the order given by Colonel Lazic. Quite a few questions were put to you which, at a certain moment, made the Chamber decide that we would verify whether the interpretation of the words you had spoken was correct or not. In two respects - and it is certainly relevant and important - there is now a proposal for a correction of the interpretation. There is even a third one but the parties are still quarreling about that -- well, the parties are not quarreling about it. The parties agree about it. But at least it has to be verified further with the -- with what we call CLSS; that is, those responsible for interpretation and translation. But I already read a portion to you. The interpretation of your words as used yesterday was, and I quote: "Because of the oral order I received from Colonel Lazic, he was there." Now has changed into: "Because of what you read, pursuant to the oral order of Colonel Lazic." So that's now the interpretation on which we'll rely. There was another portion which was corrected, or at least there's a proposal to correct it as well, and that is the part where you were recorded in the English language as having said: "It was not my decision. I was implementing an immediate order." The proposal now is to change that in: "It was not my decision. It was an implementation of an immediate order." And I think in all fairness I wanted to inform you about this because the questions put to you were very much around the words you had used, and since you apparently had problems in accepting what you were recorded as having said, the Chamber found it important enough to have it verified and now informs you that corrections are about to be made. Having said this, we'll continue to hear your evidence. Mr. Lukic, if you're ready, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We are ready, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Mr. Blagojevic.

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good day.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will just briefly summarise the corrections from the Karadzic transcript that we heard just now, and we understand that you were right in not accepting the way things had been put to you. However, my first question -- actually, I'll start from the end of today's cross-examination. You mentioned Momir Nikolic and the military police. Tell us, what kind of control did you have over Momir Nikolic on those days generally, if at all?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Over a longer period of time but at the time that we were discussing here today, I practically had no command control over Momir Nikolic and likewise the use of the military police. The platoon of the military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who made decisions at that time on how the military police platoon was supposed to be used?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that lower level, it could have been Nikolic's decisions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Yesterday, there were references to the area of responsibility. It is a fact that on some documents that term can be seen. In the area of the municipality of Bratunac, you, as commander of the 1st Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade, were you in charge of maintaining law and order in Bratunac and in other populated areas in the municipality of Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Whose task was that?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my view, how I understand that situation, primarily it should have been the task of the organised authorities in town, number one, and also the police station of the MUP. The civilian police, that is. And they have organised entities for that. That is to say, they have organised police units that ensure that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Which area? How deep? How wide? What was the area that you were responsible for?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the period that we are discussing, I had a concrete task. The brigade was in defence. I had a defence area. I was carrying out defence operations until the moment when I received orders for active attack operations, and that was the 2nd of July, 1995. The area of defence of the Bratunac Brigade means the deployment of the front line units facing the enemy. Since there was a shortage of manpower, we were mainly based on the front line because we could not have had a second or a third line because it would have required more manpower. Then also the position of the command posts of the logistics units, all of that belongs to the zone of responsibility of the brigade. So if my command post was in Kaolin - the factory that I mentioned a moment ago - then that is the area I took up together with my units and I was responsible for that area. Beyond that, no. I was under the regulations of others who were there at that point in time. Just one more sentence. This is a major weakness; namely, that for the Bratunac Brigade, this expertise was never carried out properly. Facts -- or rather, conclusions were made just like that. That is to say, without giving it proper consideration and thought.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could all other microphones please be switched off when the witness is speaking. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we have on our screens P7253, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll see the document from the 25th of May, 1995, with your name at the bottom of the document before the command of the 1st Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade. That is the day when you were appointed brigade commander, as has established until now. Before this date, where were you?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was at the command of the Drina Corps in its operations organ.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Which town?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We saw that Colonel Lazic came on the same day, arrived in Bratunac. Did you have any preparations for a take-over or did you come on this day from Vlasenica to Bratunac? Do you remember today? Did you have to assume your command straight away?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that all of that happened on that day, the 25th of May, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We saw a correction in the transcript today. Things were interpreted the way you testified here.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's look at P7256.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is another document which was issued on the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, may I just clarify. It's on the two points that a correction was made. That may not cover all of what the witness said. I just wanted to have that clearly on the record, that it's on these two points, not on other portions of the testimony of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I was not precise enough. That's exactly what I should have said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have a document sent by Mico Gavric, chief of artillery. In his document, he says that: "At 1907 hours, we opened fire on Srebrenica on Colonel Lazic's orders." Do you remember whether on that same day, when you arrived Bratunac, you saw Mico Gavric? If you can remember, of course.

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose I did see him. We were supposed to see each other that day. He was an important member of the brigade, in addition to all the other battalion commanders.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Tell us, if you remember, where did the hand-over of duties take place? Was the unit lined up?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, the unit wasn't lined up. It took place in the ops room, in a large room, which was used to process and analyse documents; i.e., it was used as the place where the brigade command worked, the largest room in the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If you had ordered Gavric to open fire, would he have written that he had received his orders from Colonel Lazic?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He would not have mentioned Lazic if he had received his orders from me. It's a -- very clear because it follows the principle of command.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On that day, the 25th of May, before you arrived, did the Bratunac Brigade have a commander; and, if so, who was that?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It did have a commander, Lieutenant-Colonel Slavko Ognjenovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did Mr. Ognjenovic attend the take-over of duties or the hand-over of duties?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And on behalf of the Drina Corps, who was there?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that Colonel Lazic was there. I don't remember anybody else.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we have another document? I don't have it recorded that we have P number for that one. It's 65 ter 06025.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This is P7255.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can see a document drafted on the same day, 25th of May, 1995. Under 1, you report that you opened fire on Srebrenica based on the verbal order of Colonel Lazic. It says here that two shells fell near the Domavija feature. What purpose did the Domavija feature serve? What was that feature?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The brigade command was privy to the intelligence according to which that feature was used by the highest command in the enclave and that it was operating from there. That's the intelligence we had at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you say "the biggest command in the enclave," what do you mean?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The command of their division, the 28th Division, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You were shown what Mr. Gavric said in the Popovic case. You were told -- or it was read to you, rather, that Gavric said that you had ordered him to fire those two projectiles. Only a few pages have been uploaded from that transcript. That's why I'm going to call up 1D05375. We'll see a broader context, or rather a bit more of what was said in the courtroom on that day. Looking from line 3 on this page --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Hasan is on her feet.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: At line 7, counsel says that it was read to him that Gavric said that "you had ordered him to fire those two projectiles." That's actually not what -- does not reflect what I read to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you then please give the exact -- if there's dispute about that, could you give exact page and line reference of yesterday's transcript, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will have to use some time for that since I did not record exact row -- lines from the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think it would be wise where --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's the same page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Where Ms. Hasan is quoting in yesterday's transcript, I would look at 33547 and/or 33548, where the -- where, I think, Ms. Hasan was reading.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Or am I wrong, Ms. Hasan?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm just looking it up myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But we don't have those pages. We just have temporary transcript on our screens.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: But that is exactly the portion we have now in the document in front of us --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... I don't know -- only I don't have that exact lines.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: -- which you uploaded separately.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I don't have exact lines what Ms. Hasan read.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I looked in yesterday's transcript and apparently we're now looking at, as my colleague tells me, at the same page from which Ms. Hasan quoted yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: If you look at the transcript what you have uploaded, Mr. Lukic, you will find that. Just there. From line 18 on that page.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm going to read what was read to you, and you will receive the correct interpretation of my words. [In English] I quote: "Q. Colonel Blagojevic was in command at this time. What was his position in May 1995, May 25th? "A. It so happened that he was there on that day. "Q. In what capacity?"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can we scroll down.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: "Q. He was the commander of the Bratunac Brigade."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But I would ask -- kindly ask to see the top of the page, line 3. Your Honour, I tried to start to read from the end of the row, line 3. And I quote from the question: "Q. It's your testimony, is it not, that you sought the authority from the Drina Corps? "A. What authority? "Q. The authority to respond by firing at the safe area. "A. I didn't seek it. There was a person from the Drina Corps there. It says it was Colonel Lazic. What I shared with you is my opinion. I did not receive a written document." Then in line 22, it was recorded that the witness, in this trial, said he was "the commander of the Bratunac Brigade," speaking of Mr. Blagojevic. But on the next page, and I kindly ask to have the next page on our screen, at line 6, there was international -- intervention by Ms. Nikolic. It says: "Your Honours, just an intervention on the translation ... the witness did not say that Blagojevic was the commander of the Bratunac Brigade, but that rather on that day he was given the duty and accepted the duty of the commander of the Bratunac Brigade." And then in line 12, Judge Kwon asked: "Are you happy with the explanation of Ms. Nikolic?" And Mr. Thayer said: "Absolutely. I understand what happened on the 25th of May, Mr. President." [Interpretation] So, Mr. Blagojevic, do you remember, as you sit here today, when was it that you effectively took over the command over the Bratunac Brigade? It was on the 25th but what time of day was it? When did you start issuing your first orders? Do you remember.

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The hand-over procedure lasted from perhaps 10.00 in the morning until the -- noon of that day. After that, I was supposed to start working in my role as the brigade commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We can see that Colonel Lazic issued an order to open fire at 7.00 in the evening that same evening. Was that in keeping with the regulations? What would you have to say to that?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that it was in compliance with the regulations.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because he represented the superior command.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Furthermore, in his testimony, Gavric said, on line 17 on the same page that we see before us, I quote: [In English] "That's why Colonel Lazic arrived. Now, I just realised when I rewound the whole film, he probably arrived to actually hand over the duties in the Bratunac Brigade on that day." And there is continuation of this on page 6 of the document we uploaded, which is 1D5375, and we need line 15 and further. And Mr. Gavric said: "I believe that on that day, Colonel Lazic came on behalf of the command of the Drina Corps and carried out the change over of the brigade commanders. From line 19, Judge Kwon asked Mr. Gavric, and I quote: "Mr. Gavric, did you ever receive an order either from Colonel Blagojevic or from Colonel Lazic to fire a shell on the town of Srebrenica? "THE WITNESS: [Interpretation] I personally don't remember whether I received an order to convey an order, whether it was ordered directly by Colonel Blagojevic or somebody else. I really can't remember. I really don't know." So, Your Honours, to have full record on the testimony of Mr. Gavric on this issue, we would offer 1D5375 into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Hasan.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: This is the testimony that's just been read out. I don't know if it's -- I understood the practice to be that if it's read in the record, that's sufficient, but I leave that for your --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps it --

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: -- consideration.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If it's just a quote, perhaps that's the original --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All we need is quotations we just read. If you think it's enough, Your Honours, we would be satisfied just have read these quotations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I was wondering whether, for example, the lines you did not read, Mr. Lukic, that Mr. Blagojevic happened to be there is relevant as well, especially in the context of the whole of it, and that is found - where was it? - I think it would for those reasons better to have the entirety of ... Therefore, Mr. Registrar, the number would be.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D966, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is admitted into evidence. The portion I referred to, Mr. Lukic, was the portion just prior to what you started reading, 26.539, is at page -- line 18 and following, the question being: "Colonel Blagojevic was in command at this time," which was then, of course, we have heard the follow-up of that. And then the answer was: "It so happened that he was there on that day." But we have now the entirety of this sequence in evidence, so you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Blagojevic, this is what I'd like to ask you: Do you remember whether on that day, the 25th, you went to the positions where the artillery pieces were and whether you saw Gavric there, or do you think that you saw him at the command? What is your recollection? Where do you think that you saw Gavric, if you remember at all?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only could have encountered him at the command. As for positions, especially artillery position, I didn't go there on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us now take a look at P7257, please. This document of the 26th of May, 1995, has already been shown to you. It a document of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the Command 28th Division. They are reporting about two mortar shells, 82 millimetres, and it is stated that Suceska was shelled using shells from an 82-millimetre mortar. How far away was Suceska from your positions?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I can assess this, the closest point from my defence lines to Suceska was perhaps 12 to 15 kilometres as the crow flies, if my recollection is correct. It's an estimate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you said that the documents say that Suceska shelled. It says the area of Suceska, which may be relevant in this context. If the witness would tell us exactly what was the closest point on his defence lines, then with a map the parties could try to seek an agreement on what the distance was rather than to rely on recollection, if it is correct. What was your closest position where you said it was perhaps 12 to 15 kilometres as the crow flies? Which point did you have in mind, which ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I had in mind was the area, the area of defence of the 3rd Battalion. And that is well known as Pribicevac here. It is mentioned here as such.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And are you saying that Pribicevac, was that directly at the separation lines?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. It's the very front line of the defence of the area of the 3rd Infantry Battalion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps the parties, with maps, could try to seek an agreement on what the distances are.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. You may recall just a couple of weeks ago we had a witness point out Suceska on a map that had the front lines on it, so perhaps Ms. Stewart can find that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if -- especially if any P number would be available so that we can just look at that time from our screens. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Blagojevic, just tell us this: I know that you're not an artilleryman, but what is the range of an 82-millimetre mortar? Do you remember now at all?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well -- well, I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If you don't know, just say you don't know.

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 3 kilometres? Up to 5 kilometres? I don't know. Maximum 3 kilometres. Sort of.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that the parties will have available any 82-millimetre mortar tables for firing which makes it clear that, depending on what propelling power is used, that the ranges are -- they may even be in evidence. I remember that. I've seen some of it earlier, and try to seek an agreement to the extent relevant here. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Hasan.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, the exhibit Mr. McCloskey was referring to is P7148.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Why did I ask you even some of these indubitable questions about mortars and their ranges? Now I'm going to ask you something else. To the best of your knowledge, first of all, did you have 82-millimetre mortars? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: To the best of your knowledge, from the positions where these mortars were, could you fire at the area of Suceska or rather the village of Bucinovici, if you know where that is.

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think we never could have done that and we never did that. It's far away.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We now need P7260.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Before that, just for the record, I'm going to give a number. The Prosecution showed you -- well, I didn't write the number down, but it was 65 ter 25386. There was a reference to the shelling of Tuzla and the question was whether you knew about that. How far away is Tuzla from the place where you were?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At least 100 kilometres away.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And the number is now P7258.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] P7259 was also shown to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So I'd need that on the screen, first of all. I do apologise. I went a bit too far ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Again, this is a report. This time this is a UN report on -- about the day when you are assuming your duties at the Bratunac Brigade when you are arriving from Vlasenica to Bratunac. And this report says that: "After the air strikes of 25th May 1995, all safe areas less Zepa have been shelled ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now in relation to that -- I'm not going ask you anything yet until I show you the next document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now we need P7260.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Already in the first paragraph, you can see that on that first day when you assumed command of the Bratunac Brigade on the 25th of May, 1995: "In the afternoon hours there were operations carried out by NATO aircraft, which are part of UNPROFOR, against facilities of the Army of Republika Srpska. The Army of Republika Srpska responded adequately by conducting operations against selected targets. However, it is to be expected that Muslim forces in co-operation with UNPROFOR will continue operations against military targets in Republika Srpska."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you added one word, "adequately," which is not to be seen in this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Maybe it's not seen in English version, but this is original in B/C/S and it says "adequately." Here, it's the fourth line, the fifth word, in B/C/S "adekvatno," so probably this should be revisited translation-wise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The document was produced by the Prosecution, so therefore I think it's upon the Prosecution to have the translation verified; specifically, in relation to the issue mentioned by Mr. Lukic a second ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next document that we need to be displayed on our screens is the next one in the sequence of the Prosecution, P7261.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: A report was read out to you from the area of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps, number 1, here, where it says, on that same day, the 25th of May, 1995, when the NATO air strikes started, when the Command of the Drina Corps is cautioning that it is to be expected that Muslim forces, together with UNPROFOR, are going to continue operations, in this document, in paragraph 1, I'm going to quote it now, I'm going to read it out. "The enemy: Along the entire defence line of the corps, ... has incessantly fired from infantry weapons, artillery pieces, mortars of all calibres, and snipers." Then further on we see: "They fired mortars and howitzers of 105 millimetres." And also it says: "They fired from NATO aircraft (using air bombs) against the area of Jahorinski Potok, over the warehouse of the 27th pob ... at a distance of 500 metres." Mr. Blagojevic, that day and the days after that, could you notice in that area where you were - that is to say, the area of Bratunac - could you notice that there was co-ordinated action between NATO air force and the enemy forces of the 28th Division?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, we followed that all the time. This was action in concert and co-ordinated action, and it was pronounced. And how? Vis-à-vis the forces of the Army of Republika Srpska, my brigade included.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Today do you remember that first day, the following day, as for the positions of your forces that you started commanding from the 25th of May, 1995, was fire opened against these positions? Fire from the town of Srebrenica? Fire from the enclave of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Fire from the enclave of Srebrenica was opened permanently in different periods against the positions of the brigade, and mostly in different ways. Mostly by infantry. And the other weapons they had available. Because it is a fact that they had not been demilitarised. Likewise, they carried out other active operations, ambushes, incursions, that were a constant threat to the safety and security of the members of the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Blagojevic. Let's go back to D303, which was shown to you. This is your order for active combat dated 5 July 1995. Now that we have identified the document, let me first ask you this: When it comes to the drafting of this document, did you do it on your own or did you have assistance from the staff who helped you with that?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this very specific case, I co-operated with some of the people in the command of the brigade; the Chief of Staff, the operative, the engineer, chief of engineers, the logistics chief. I drafted the order together with them. I assessed the situation --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you also say the artilleryman?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. The artillery guy.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now let's look at bullet point 6 on page 4 in English and on page 3 in B/C/S. The Prosecutor showed you the same paragraph in her examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, I'm interested in 6.2. [In English] Can we have the next page in B/C/S. We have the page in English. No, no, we had the good page in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Looking at 6.2 where there is a reference to the 128-millimetre rocket-launcher platoon, who sends whom the proposal for the use of a certain platoon?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the brigade, it would be the chief of artillery. He prepared the proposal and he submitted to me, the brigade commander. And that happens in a predetermined sequence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just bear with me for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm trying to keep my re-examination short since you've already answered some of the questions that I have prepared for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, if you want to further reduce it, you could try to find out during the break how to do it. Unless you would say I'll be finished in a few minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think I could cut it down drastically if I have a break time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And meanwhile, I invite the parties to have look at P7148 and tell the Chamber what the grid, the squares on that map are.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: The grid squares should be 2 kilometres square.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 2 kilometres. 2 kilometres square.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I can't see that on the exhibit itself, I think. We'll have a look at it so as to be better able to understand the testimony of the witness. We'll take a break first, Mr. Lukic, and then we'll hear from you how much time you would still need after the break. Witness, you may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I take it that we'll be able to conclude the testimony of this witness today?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honour. I don't need much time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I'm also looking at Ms. Hasan because ...

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then, still for the next witness, if he is on stand by, would he need to remain on stand by?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: He is on stand by.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And is there a fair chance we would have more than five minutes with him? If you need only two or three minutes or five minutes and Ms. Hasan doesn't need any more than another five minutes, then of course we could still start with the witness. So let's try to achieve that. We take a break and will resume at --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I can tell you, I probably don't have more than ten minutes, maybe five.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's appreciated. We'll take a break, and we'll resume at quarter to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now let's look at two more documents. P1694 is the first one. I'll have some questions for you. This document was issued by Colonel Ignjat Milanovic on the 15th of July, 1995. In this document, he suggested that you should be appointed as the commander of all the forces engaged in the scouring of the terrain. That's his proposal number 1. And then you were shown P1696. The date is 16 July, 1995, your name is typed up, and you gave us an account of each of the bullet points, especially in response to Judge Orie's questions, and you said that those things did not actually take place. You said that a supposition is a normal thing. What is a supposition? Do you have a definition of that term?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A supposition is something that is used in war games when one wishes to simulate a situation in order to achieve certain things or achieve a change of situation. In that sense and through that you can assess the level of preparedness of a command, its level of training to perform certain duties or to carry out a certain task.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If I may just get an explanation here, please. Then would that be in a report that reports things that have happened? Because this report is telling us about things that have happened, not that are being supposed or that are being planned.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's the way I understand the term "supposition." This is what I wanted to achieve.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yeah, but this is a daily combat report. It is reporting what has taken place that day, not what is supposed to happen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've just told you. If this is recorded, then I did it myself. You can see that some things have been crossed out in handwriting, which means that I wrote those things myself. You can actually see my handwriting here.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's on page 3 in this document, Your Honour, if you want to see that in writing. In B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Nothing in the English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have access to any pages we want to look at, but thank you for guiding us to page 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: This one we are seeing for the first time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, the problem is not, Witness, perhaps, that we do not understand what a supposition is, but we do not understand how in such a report you'd use suppositions rather than events that had happened, because the other side who received the report might be greatly misled if they receive reports A happened and they have to understand that as, well, A could have happened, but B could have happened as well. That's not what we have seen often in this type of reports, and that's what triggers so much our curiosity on how this works.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Blagojevic, could you look at the handwriting on the bottom of that page. Is this sentence: "During the day the brigade commander visited all units," is that still legible there, or did you cross that out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, but I added, as you can see. There's an arrow pointing in the direction of that part of the text.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. That is in your own handwriting, as I understood you. And --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: -- it refers to this text we were discussing several -- several times today: "During the day the brigade commander visited all units," and then they are listed. And this is contained in your own handwriting in this letter on left-hand side, on the bottom; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It's not crossed out. You may proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's the same handwriting, all of this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's all understood. You may proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I would just show this witness next document. That's 65 ter number 04238.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Blagojevic, you see the document before you. The Command of the 1st Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade, dated 16 July, 1995, on the same day as the document entitled: "Combat Report." It says here: "A deployment of the battalion into combat activity area, order:" In the first paragraph, we can read: "On the basis of the order issued by the commander of the Drina Corps on the 16th of July, 1995, and for the purpose of timely preparation of the unit and its deployment in the area of combat activity, I hereby order... "

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see all that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Under 1, it says: "The commander of the 1st infantry battalion ..."

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, infantry battalion, that's what PB stands.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: "... will immediately pull out the whole battalion from its area of deployment and prepare it for combat activity." Where was the deployment area of the 1st Infantry Battalion? Can you remember that?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It had its defence sector which remained after the previously mentioned order. After that, its task was to search the terrain in a certain area. Again, the area was defined in the previous document. And then after searching the terrain, they entered the stage of forming the march alignment to start marching towards Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Under 6, it says: "The commander of the 1st Infantry Battalion shall be responsible for preparing the battalion to complete its task." What was your role during those preparation? Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My role was decisive. The most important one. That's why I joined them on their mission the following day.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That would have been my next question. We can see under 5 that: "The unit is to be fully prepared for the march at 0700 hours on the 17th July, 1995." You say that you joined them. You joined the battalion. Where did you go with them?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went in the sector called Podzeplje, south of Han Pijesak, if I remember it well. I went into that sector in the vicinity of Zepa enclave. From its north western side. I can't give you the exact location. I would have to consult a map. But in any case, it was the Podzeplje sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How long did you stay there?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until the end of August, up to 25th or 26th of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: August or July?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hold on. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until the end of those activities surrounding Zepa. I know it lasted for a long time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And let's look at the signature at the very bottom of the document. Do you recognise it?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the signature on the order?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is my document. I drafted it and I signed it as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Blagojevic, thank you. This is all we had for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Only, Your Honours, we would offer this document into evidence, 65 ter 04238.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D967, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D967 is admitted. Ms. Hasan, any further questions?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Very briefly, Your Honours. Could we call up 65 ter 5815. Further cross-examination by Ms. Hasan:

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And you were asked at transcript page 53 about the area of responsibility. And we actually do have the original. This is a map.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Perhaps with the assistance of the usher, we can hand that to Mr. Blagojevic to look at. And to the Defence and Your Honours as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, in view of what happens now, the next witness can be excused. I feel sorry for him, but ... yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And just for the screens, that's 65 ter 5815.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could it be given to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And to the Defence first. Unless, Mr. Lukic, you waive your right to inspect the map.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: There is a translation for this map, I assume it's just -- takes a bit of time to appear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you put your question to the witness, then...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Blagojevic, you've taken a look at the map, and you see that -- well, just to inform you, this is a map that was taken from the Bratunac Brigade command in 1998. And there's an area you see there shaded in a pale yellow colour. That's the area of responsibility of the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. If we are talking about that period, 1995, no. This is a map that was made in 1992 in the month of November when the Bratunac Brigade was established, and it was made for completely different purposes and on the basis of completely different elements and facts. In 1995, totally different elements were valid; that is to say, the rules and regulations that applied in the Army of Republika Srpska. This does not refer to the period that we are discussing. This is November 1992. That is the period. And that is quite different from what the situation was in 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You've told us that now three times. But could you then please indicate, was it smaller in 1995 - and I'm talking about the geographical area, because we're looking at the map - was it smaller, was it larger where parts were not any more in the area of responsibility of the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade? Where were there areas which may have been added to what was the situation in 1992? Could you please be concrete on the matter.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The situation in 1995 was very concrete. That was the zone of defence of the Bratunac Brigade vis-à-vis the enclave of Srebrenica, and it was defined through orders of the superior command, or rather -- please allow me. The next order for active operations. So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, what we -- we see a map and we see highlighted a certain geographical area where it says areas of responsibility of the Light Infantry Brigade. You say in 1992 it was not the same as in 1995. Could you tell us, apart from all kind of decisions, was it smaller, was it larger? Are you able with a pen to more or less put on this map what was actually the situation in 1995?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can. In terms of the defence sector facing the enclave of Srebrenica 1995, much, much smaller. It is very defined as compared to this map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You are constantly talking about a defence sector. I'm talking - and that is the question - is about the area of responsibility of the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade. Not anything else about defence elements or ... was that different in 1995?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, substantially so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I leave it in your hands, Ms. Hasan, to find out with the witness or at least to elicit from the witness what he thinks was the area of responsibility in 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So we agree, then, that there was an area of responsibility of the Bratunac Brigade in July of 1995. Now, the geographical borders of that area of responsibility, can you briefly set those out? You were the commander. You surely know where those borders were. And let's begin with the north, and we can work or way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Hasan, wouldn't it be best that he has a pen and that he can say where the borders now were?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could a pen be provided to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the marking can be done on the B/C/S version only.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I? May I say something about this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, we'd first like you to mark where the boundaries were in 1995. May I take it July 1995, Ms. Hasan?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: July 1995.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, I can't see here where the border of the enclave is. I cannot draw the front part. I have to draw the front part, the front line, the first line of defence of my units, and I cannot do it here. This is not a working map. This is not a map to be worked with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Blagojevic, ignore the enclaves. They are in -- obviously in the middle of the map. The outer border of the Bratunac Brigade, this is the question. Is that exactly the area of responsibility? Ignore the enclaves at the defence lines.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judge, sir, the zone of defence of my brigade is delineated on the front part with the defence line of the units facing the enemy. Then there's the right flank and the left flank. In depth, in depth. Now I'm moving this way into my own territory. The depth is determined by the disposition of the firing positions, the logistics units, and the command posts of the units. That's the area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think you are not understanding the question put by Ms. Hasan, by the Presiding Judge, and by me. Look at the map. Is the Drina the border of the zone of responsibility of your brigade, to the east?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Not at all. I cannot base the zone of defence on this kind of surface. No. Impossible. I've never done any such thing in practice. And on the basis of the regulations that were in force at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any way you could -- could mark on a map where the Zvornik Brigade and the -- and the Bratunac Brigade, where the border between the two zones of responsibility was? So as to say the one side of the line it's the Zvornik Brigade, the other side of the line is the Bratunac Brigade. Is there any way for you to do that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is it possible to enlarge --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I had no connection with the Zvornik Brigade. We were not adjacent. With the Milici Brigade on the right and to the left with the Skelani Battalion, in a way. With the Zvornik Brigade, I had nothing to do with them whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you mark on the map whatever borders you could draw between your area of responsibility and the area of responsibility of the adjacent brigades.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is very hard to do it here because the scale is so small. You have other maps here, probably.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we enlarge part of the map so that at least -- get it a little bit more in the centre and have it enlarged. We ... And just the area of the responsibility, if we could move up a bit, and now move down slightly. Little bit more. Little bit more. Perhaps a little bit. And enlarge it slightly again. Okay. Could you do it on the basis of what we have on our screen now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Over here, I cannot decipher the name of a single village here. You should bear in mind that I have a bad eye. I can barely see with one eye, so maybe you should give me a map with a different scale, 1:50.000.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Hasan, we now know all the problems the witness is facing in doing what he is supposed to do. I suggest that we try to do it in the first 15 minutes tomorrow morning, because this will not resolve in anything in the next ten minutes, if at all necessary. That's a different matter. You also could consider whether or not you could do without all this.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: It's difficult to tell how useful of an exercise it will be to try again tomorrow. I would --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but you have to make up your mind on the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would ask the witness that, in fact, he is trying to mark the -- which he keeps repeating, the defence zone and not the area of responsibility. That's correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But then again, the witness says I can't read any name on it. But let's check with him. Would you be able, on the basis of what you have in front of you now, to draw the borders of the defence zone of your brigade? Or is it still too small?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judge, sir, this is a key question for me. I wish to give the right answer and a full answer to this question. This is the main question in this entire game.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, it's not a game, perhaps. But Ms. Hasan, you are now at a point where you have to decide whether or not to provide the witness with a map he can work it and do that tomorrow morning or to waive or to withdraw these questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I won't withdraw the questions if I can put one final question to him and then I can just end the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Blagojevic, the reason, in fact, that you're refusing to recognise the area of responsibility as marked on this map is because you don't want any responsibility for what took place within that -- within that area in July of 1995. That's correct?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: God forbid, this has nothing to do with the truth. This is nonsense. I am just speaking about facts.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I'd then just offer 65 ter 5815 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P7265, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is admitted into evidence. No further questions? So you do withdraw the other questions, Ms. Hasan?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: No, I withdraw it and -- it's our position that he is refusing to mark the area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, no, that's fine. But the marking questions, et cetera, they are now off? Yes. That's what I call withdrawal of a question. Mr. Mladic should refrain from making all kind of gestures. No -- Mr. Mladic, you do it again. It's ... Mr. Lukic, we will adjourn for the day, but this concludes your testimony, Mr. Blagojevic. Therefore, I would like to thank you very much for coming a long way to The Hague and for having answered many questions that were put to you by the parties and by the Bench. I wish you a safe return home again. And Mr. Domazet is thanked for his services provided to the witness. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I put on the record that Mr. Mladic was saluting the witness, which he's supposed not to do, and the Chamber will consider whether misbehaviour at the end of the testimony of a witness should not result in exclusion for the next witness or at least have consequences for the proceedings. We adjourn for the day and will resume tomorrow, Wednesday, the 25th of March, 9.30 in the morning, in this same courtroom, I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 25th day of March, 2015, at 9.30 a.m. 24 25
